caption: 01 · AUTHOR — Who made the photograph?. Record the photographer, capture date and time, file origin, embedded metadata, assignment, employer, commissioning party, and whether a statutory work-made-for-hire theory is actually supported. Payment alone is not the test.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who made the photograph? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · TRANSFER — Did ownership or an exclusive right move?. Locate the signed writing, identify the rights transferred, territory, media, duration, exclusivity, sublicensing, credit, editing, archive, and termination terms. A delivery folder, invoice, or social post may be relevant evidence but is not automatically a complete transfer instrument.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping did ownership or an exclusive right move? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · PERMISSION STACK — What else governs use?. Separate copyright from accreditation terms, publication license, model agreement, venue rules, embargo, trademark presentation, publicity or privacy law, and contractual restrictions. The answer may change with use, territory, and audience.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what else governs use? within Who Owns a Runway Image?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · PUBLISH — Can the exact use be shown?. Before publishing, bind the exact image or clip to its source record, permitted use, crop or edit, credit, caption, alt text, license evidence, expiration, takedown route, and counsel decision where the stack remains uncertain.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

caption: A permissions system can become so risk-averse that it erases photographers, models, and makers from public memory. The answer is not casual reuse; it is better licensing, clearer credits, fairer agreements, durable records, and a proportionate review process that preserves access without laundering uncertainty.
